newsitem.title: USA: Clinton gets good marks for Mideast - Reuters poll.
newsitem.headline: Clinton gets good marks for Mideast - Reuters poll.

text.p: Voters give President Bill Clinton fairly high marks for his handling of the Israeli-Palestinian crisis in a Reuters poll on Friday that put the president 14.3 percentage points ahead of Republican Bob Dole.
The survey of 948 likely voters, conducted by John Zogby Group International, is a rolling average of polling results from Tuesday through Thursday and carries a 3.3 percentage point margin of error.
Asked how they rate Clinton on his handling of the Mideast crisis, 9 percent called it "excellent", 33 percent said it was "good", 29 percent said it was "fair" and 14 percent rated it "poor".

Dole blasted the White House gathering of Middle East leaders which Clinton convened to rescue the faltering Arab-Israeli peace process. Dole said the summit was a hastily-convened "photo op" called by Clinton with a eye on the election.
In a speech on Thursday, Dole widened his attack to encompass the entire Clinton foreign policy record.
"The Clinton administration's foreign policy is rudderless and illusionary," Dole said.
In the poll, Clinton led with 47.5 percent, ahead of Dole with 33.2 percent. Reform Party candidate Ross Perot's support dropped to 4.4 percent, its lowest level yet.
"While Clinton did not gain directly as a result of the Middle East summit, Dole appears to have hurt himself by interjecting a partisan view during a sensitive period," said pollster John Zogby.

With both candidates looking ahead to the two presidential debates, the first of which takes place on Sunday, the poll found that attitudes had hardened and that if anything Dole's support was slightly softer than Clinton's.
Some 63 percent of Clinton backers said their support for the president was "very strong", 29 percent said it was "somewhat strong" and 7 percent said it was "not strong."
For Dole, the equivalent figures were: 60 percent very strong, 30 percent somewhat strong and 10 percent not strong.
Asked which party's candidate they intended to vote for in their congressional district, 34 percent said Democrats and 35.4 percent said Republicans.
